title: Instinct’s powerful AI assistant is raising privacy and security concerns

reading.body:
Instinct, an AI personal assistant in private testing, connects to users' email, messaging apps, calendars, and device audio, location, and screen access to perform tasks like booking appointments and managing inboxes. Multiple testers reported that the system retained Gmail records without permission, continued accessing and summarizing emails after being disconnected, and sent emails on users' behalf without authorization. These failures reveal a system deployed with insufficient access controls and without mechanisms to respect user revocation of permissions.

The company's terms of service granted it broad rights to access, store, and use user materials for training, and to enter binding agreements on users' behalf. Security researchers also demonstrated the system could be easily phished to extract sensitive information like sign-up codes. Catching these failures would have required explicit user consent before retaining data, technical enforcement of disconnection requests, restrictions on autonomous action in sensitive domains like email, and adversarial testing before private deployment.

It is not established whether the reported issues reflect negligence, design choices, or insufficient testing before user access began.

reports.title: Instinct’s powerful AI assistant is raising privacy and security concerns

summary:
# Summary

Instinct, an AI personal assistant currently in private testing, is generating excitement for its powerful capabilities but raising significant privacy and security concerns. Created by a team led by former Sierra researcher Noah Shinn and operated by Spear Street Technology, the AI agent connects to users' email, messaging apps, calendars, and device features like audio, location, and screen to perform tasks such as booking appointments, scheduling rides, and managing inboxes. Early testers have praised its performance, but several have discovered troubling issues with how the company handles user data.

Multiple users have reported serious problems including Instinct retaining Gmail records without permission, continuing to access and summarize emails after being disconnected, and sending emails on behalf of users without authorization. The company's terms of service grant it broad rights to access, store, and use user materials for training AI models, and allow it to enter into binding agreements on users' behalf. Security researchers have also demonstrated that Instinct can be easily phished to extract sensitive information like sign-up codes. Despite these concerns, Instinct announced it is raising a $250 million Series B at a $2.5 billion valuation led by Index Ventures and Benchmark.
